chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Meeting W. C. Handy in Montgomery
summary: As a boy he met Handy at a concert in Montgomery, was struck by the production and the big brass section, and thinks it influenced him to be a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: -- piano for W. C. Handy, as a demonstrator. Did you ever meet W. C. Handy?
Yeah, I met him once in Montgomery. They did a concert there and that was the thrill of my life.
The one thing, what a tremendous gentle-

man he was. This is what -- you know. And that was the one thing I remembered about him. I didn't get a chance to, you know -- I was a kid (unintelligible), I just met him. But I went to the concert. I had never seen anything like this before in my life. This is -- was a production.

I mean, it was just a big band, there was a polish, it was a -- I had never seen a production like this with -- everything was like it was a concert. And I had never seen a real big brass section, and the drums with the bells and, you know, it was just fascinating. And to think that my mother had worked for him was something, you know. So that -- that might have influenced me to be a musician too, I don't know. I'm sure it did. You know.
You wanted to be a part of that (in-- audible).
Yeah. Well, just, you know, I admired them so, and I always wanted to play. And as I said, I'd been around music all my life, you know, so --
